# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` is a boolean that **defaults to `True`** — existing/created articles are public unless explicitly saved as a draft.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Base queryset is filtered to `is_published=True` so **drafts never leak into the global, following, or tag feeds**. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets.
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Fresh Post", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)


class PublishDefaultPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DEFAULT-002: property — any article saved without
    touching the publish flag is published.

    Mirrors SlugStabilityPropertyTest: each Hypothesis example runs in its own
    rolled-back transaction, so a fresh author + article per example is
    collision-free regardless of the (arbitrary) title.
    """

    @given(title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_new_article_is_published(self, title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="pub@example.com", username="pubby", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(article.is_published)


class MarkdownFilterTest(TestCase):
    def test_renders_markdown_and_sanitizes(self):
        html = render_markdown("# Hello\n\n**bold**")
        self.assertIn("<h1>", html)
        self.assertIn("<strong>", html)

    def test_strips_unsafe_html(self):
        html = render_markdown("<script>alert(1)</script>ok")
        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)


class HomeViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        cache.clear()
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.art1 = make_article(self.alice, title="Post One", tags=["python"])
        self.art2 = make_article(self.bob, title="Post Two", tags=["django"])

    def test_anonymous_home_shows_all(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "global")

    def test_tag_query_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?tag=python")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "tag")

    def test_tag_url_path_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("tag", args=["django"]))
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post One")

    def test_following_feed_anonymous_redirects_to_login(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_following_feed_authenticated(self):
        self.alice.followers.add(self.bob)  # bob follows alice

    def test_global_feed_excludes_drafts(self):

    def test_following_feed_excludes_drafts(self):

    def test_tag_feed_excludes_drafts(self):

        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Draft Tagged")

    def test_invalid_page_defaults_to_one(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?page=bogus")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["page"], 1)

    def test_htmx_request_returns_partial(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"), HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("partials/feed_content.html", [t.name for t in resp.templates if t.name])

    def test_global_feed_orders_newest_first(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_full_page_load_renders_full_template(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_feed_shows_at_most_ten_articles_per_page(self):

Feature: Authoring and favoriting articles
  As an author
  I want to create, edit, and delete my own articles, and favorite others' work
  So that I can publish my writing and signal which articles I value

  Authoring is restricted to the article's own author. Favoriting is open to
  any signed-in reader and toggles on each action. Both demand authentication;
  an anonymous visitor is always sent to sign in first.

  Rule: Only a signed-in user may reach the article editor

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor is redirected away from the new-article editor
      When an anonymous visitor opens the new-article editor
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-002
    Scenario: A signed-in author opens the new-article editor
      Given a signed-in author
      When they open the new-article editor
      Then the article editor is presented

  Rule: Publishing an article records its title, summary, body, tags, and author

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-001
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article titled "New Title" with a summary, a body, and the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article is created with that author
      And its summary and body are recorded as entered
      And it carries the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-002
    Scenario: Tag entries are trimmed and blank entries discarded
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article carries exactly the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-003
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with no tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with an empty tag list
      Then the article is created with no tags

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-004
    Scenario: After publishing, the author lands on the new article
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish a valid article
      Then they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-005
    Scenario: An article cannot be published without a title
      Given a signed-in author
      When they submit the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may edit their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot edit the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to open the edit editor for that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-002
    Scenario: The author's editor is pre-filled with the current article
      Given a signed-in author with an article titled "Edit Me" tagged "python"
      When they open the edit editor for that article
      Then the editor is pre-filled with "Edit Me"
      And the editor is pre-filled with the tag "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-003
    Scenario: An author edits the summary, body, and tags of their article
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with a new summary, a new body, and the tags "rust"
      Then the article's summary and body are updated
      And the article carries exactly the tag "rust"
      And they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-004
    Scenario: A saved edit cannot leave the title empty
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may delete their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot delete the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to delete that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-002
    Scenario: An author deletes their own article
      Given a signed-in author with an article
      When they delete that article
      Then the article no longer exists
      And they are returned to the home feed

  Rule: Favoriting requires sign-in and toggles on each action

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot favorite an article
      When an anonymous visitor tries to favorite an article
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-002
    Scenario: Favoriting then favoriting again removes the favorite
      Given a signed-in reader and an article they have not favorited
      When the reader favorites the article
      Then the article counts the reader among its favorites
      When the reader favorites the article again
      Then the article no longer counts the reader among its favorites

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-003
    Scenario: After a non-HTMX favorite the reader returns to the article
      Given a signed-in reader and an article

      Then they are returned to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-004

# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` is a boolean that **defaults to `True`** — existing/created articles are public unless explicitly saved as a draft.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Base queryset is filtered to `is_published=True` so **drafts never leak into the global, following, or tag feeds**. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets. The "my articles" tab is a public surface and lists **published articles only** — an author's drafts never appear there (they live in the `?feed=drafts` feed).
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).

class ArticleCreateViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()

    def test_anonymous_redirects(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_create"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_get_renders_form(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_create"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_post_creates_article_with_tags(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "New Title", "description": "d", "body": "b", "tags": "python,  django  , "},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        art = Article.objects.get(title="New Title")
        self.assertEqual(art.author, self.alice)
        self.assertEqual(art.summary, "d")
        self.assertEqual(art.content, "b")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(t.name for t in art.tags.all()), ["django", "python"])

    def test_post_creates_article_without_tags(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "No Tags", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(Article.objects.get(title="No Tags").tags.count(), 0)

    def test_post_invalid_form_rerenders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_create"), {"title": "", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_post_redirects_to_new_article_detail(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "Land Here", "description": "d", "body": "b", "tags": ""},
        )
        art = Article.objects.get(title="Land Here")
        self.assertRedirects(resp, reverse("article_detail", args=[art.slug]))


class ArticleEditViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.article = make_article(self.alice, title="Edit Me", tags=["python"])

    def test_non_author_gets_404(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

    def test_get_prefills_form(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Edit Me")
        self.assertContains(resp, "python")

    def test_post_updates_article(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]),
            {"title": "Edit Me", "description": "new desc", "body": "new body", "tags": "rust"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.article.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.article.summary, "new desc")
        self.assertEqual(self.article.content, "new body")
        self.assertEqual([t.name for t in self.article.tags.all()], ["rust"])

    def test_post_invalid_form_rerenders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        resp = self.client.post(
            reverse("article_edit", args=[self.article.slug]),
            {"title": "", "description": "", "body": "", "tags": ""},
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)


class ArticleDeleteViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.article = make_article(self.alice, title="Delete Me")

    def test_non_author_gets_404(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.post(reverse("article_delete", args=[self.article.slug]))

The e2e helper never sends a publish field — it just clicks "Publish Article" and expects a **published** article. So the robust design is a **`draft` checkbox, unchecked by default**: an absent field means published, which keeps every existing unit test and the e2e suite green by construction. I'll record this refinement in decisions.md, then TDD.

Let me update the decision record first:

     single "Publish Article" button.
   Rationale: keeps the pinned "Publish Article" button and a single save path;
     checkbox default = published preserves current behavior. Rendered `checked`
     so a real browser (Playwright e2e) submits `published=on` and keeps creating
     published articles — the existing suite stays green.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Two submit buttons ("Publish" / "Save Draft"): keys logic off which button
       was pressed; more template + view branching for no real gain.
     - A published/draft <select>: heavier UI than a boolean needs.

     `createArticle`/`editArticle` never touches a publish control — it just

       semantics.
     - Two submit buttons ("Publish" / "Save Draft"): keys logic off which button

     - A published/draft <select>: heavier UI than a boolean needs.

# Decisions — article-drafts

All resolved. Zero open `?` markers.

✓ Drafts discovery surface
   Chose: a feed tab `?feed=drafts` handled in `_feed_queryset`, mirroring `following`.
   Rationale: `apps/articles/CLAUDE.md` names `_feed_queryset` as *the* seam for
     new feed types and lists "drafts" by name. Reuses pagination, HTMX fragment
     rendering, and the empty-state partial for free.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - A third profile tab ("My Articles / Favorited / Drafts"): profile is a
       public surface keyed by username; a private drafts tab there is awkward
       (must branch on is_self) and duplicates feed plumbing.
     - A standalone /drafts page: new view + template + pagination, all of which
       the feed pipeline already provides.

✓ Editor publish/draft control
   Chose: one "Published" checkbox, checked by default, alongside the existing
     single "Publish Article" button.
   Rationale: keeps the pinned "Publish Article" button and a single save path;
     checkbox default = published preserves current behavior. Rendered `checked`
     so a real browser (Playwright e2e) submits `published=on` and keeps creating
     published articles — the existing suite stays green.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Two submit buttons ("Publish" / "Save Draft"): keys logic off which button
       was pressed; more template + view branching for no real gain.
     - A published/draft <select>: heavier UI than a boolean needs.

✓ Publish-flag default
   Chose: model default `True` (published), form field default checked.
   Rationale: the hard requirement — existing articles must stay visible. A
     default-True column backfills every existing row as published in the
     migration with no data step.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - default False + data migration flipping all existing rows: same end state,
       more moving parts, risk of missing rows created between deploy steps.

✓ Public-surface filtering scope
   Chose: filter `is_published=True` in global, following, and tag feeds AND the
     profile "My Articles" tab.
   Rationale: those are the surfaces that list a user's articles to *readers*;
     all must hide drafts to honor "drafts are private to their author."
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Feeds only, leave profile: profile "My Articles" would leak an author's
       drafts to any visitor of their profile.

✓ Draft detail-page access
   Chose: the author may view their own draft's detail page; everyone else
     (incl. anonymous) gets the existing 404.
   Rationale: create/edit redirect to the detail page; the author must be able to
     land there. Non-authors must not read unpublished work by guessing the slug.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - 404 for everyone incl. author: breaks the post-save redirect for drafts.
     - Public draft detail: leaks unpublished work via direct URL.

✓ Index on is_published
   Chose: no DB index.
   Rationale: YAGNI at this data scale; feeds already filter+order on indexed
     columns. Revisit only under a measured query-perf trigger.
   Rejected alternatives:
     - Partial/plain index now: premature optimization, extra migration surface.

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Fresh Post", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)


class PublishDefaultPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DEFAULT-002: property — any article saved without
    touching the publish flag is published.

    Mirrors SlugStabilityPropertyTest: each Hypothesis example runs in its own
    rolled-back transaction, so a fresh author + article per example is
    collision-free regardless of the (arbitrary) title.
    """

    @given(title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_new_article_is_published(self, title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="pub@example.com", username="pubby", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(article.is_published)


class MarkdownFilterTest(TestCase):
    def test_renders_markdown_and_sanitizes(self):
        html = render_markdown("# Hello\n\n**bold**")
        self.assertIn("<h1>", html)
        self.assertIn("<strong>", html)

    def test_strips_unsafe_html(self):
        html = render_markdown("<script>alert(1)</script>ok")
        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)


class HomeViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        cache.clear()
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.art1 = make_article(self.alice, title="Post One", tags=["python"])
        self.art2 = make_article(self.bob, title="Post Two", tags=["django"])

    def test_anonymous_home_shows_all(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "global")

    def test_tag_query_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?tag=python")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "tag")

    def test_tag_url_path_filters(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("tag", args=["django"]))
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post One")

    def test_following_feed_anonymous_redirects_to_login(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_following_feed_authenticated(self):
        self.alice.followers.add(self.bob)  # bob follows alice
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "following")

    def test_global_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        make_article(self.alice, title="Secret Draft", is_published=False)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Secret Draft")
        self.assertNotIn("Secret Draft", [a.title for a in resp.context["articles"]])

    def test_following_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        self.alice.followers.add(self.bob)  # bob follows alice
        make_article(self.alice, title="Alice Draft", is_published=False)
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Alice Draft")

    def test_tag_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        make_article(self.alice, title="Draft Tagged", tags=["python"], is_published=False)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?tag=python")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Draft Tagged")

    def test_invalid_page_defaults_to_one(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?page=bogus")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["page"], 1)

    def test_htmx_request_returns_partial(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"), HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("partials/feed_content.html", [t.name for t in resp.templates if t.name])

    def test_global_feed_orders_newest_first(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        articles = list(resp.context["articles"])
        self.assertEqual([a.pk for a in articles], [self.art2.pk, self.art1.pk])

    def test_full_page_load_renders_full_template(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("articles/home.html", [t.name for t in resp.templates if t.name])

    def test_feed_shows_at_most_ten_articles_per_page(self):
        for i in range(11):
            make_article(self.alice, title=f"Bulk Post {i}")
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(resp.context["articles"]), 10)

    def test_feed_offers_all_tags(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        tag_names = sorted(t.name for t in resp.context["tags"])
        self.assertEqual(tag_names, ["django", "python"])

    def test_new_tag_available_after_article_saved(self):
        # Prime the cache with the current tag set.
        self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        self.client.post(
            reverse("article_create"),
            {"title": "Tagged Fresh", "description": "d", "body": "b", "tags": "rust"},
        )
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertIn("rust", [t.name for t in resp.context["tags"]])

class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)


class PublishDefaultPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DEFAULT-002: property — any article saved without
    touching the publish flag is published.

    Mirrors SlugStabilityPropertyTest: each Hypothesis example runs in its own
    rolled-back transaction, so a fresh author + article per example is
    collision-free regardless of the (arbitrary) title.
    """

    @given(title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_new_article_is_published(self, title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="pub@example.com", username="pubby", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(article.is_published)

Feature: Authoring and favoriting articles
  As an author
  I want to create, edit, and delete my own articles, and favorite others' work
  So that I can publish my writing and signal which articles I value

  Authoring is restricted to the article's own author. Favoriting is open to
  any signed-in reader and toggles on each action. Both demand authentication;
  an anonymous visitor is always sent to sign in first.

  Rule: Only a signed-in user may reach the article editor

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor is redirected away from the new-article editor
      When an anonymous visitor opens the new-article editor
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDITOR-ACCESS-002
    Scenario: A signed-in author opens the new-article editor
      Given a signed-in author
      When they open the new-article editor
      Then the article editor is presented

  Rule: Publishing an article records its title, summary, body, tags, and author

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-001
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article titled "New Title" with a summary, a body, and the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article is created with that author
      And its summary and body are recorded as entered
      And it carries the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-002
    Scenario: Tag entries are trimmed and blank entries discarded
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with the tags "python,  django  , "
      Then the article carries exactly the tags "django" and "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-003
    Scenario: An author publishes an article with no tags
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish an article with an empty tag list
      Then the article is created with no tags

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-004
    Scenario: After publishing, the author lands on the new article
      Given a signed-in author
      When they publish a valid article
      Then they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-CREATE-005
    Scenario: An article cannot be published without a title
      Given a signed-in author
      When they submit the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may edit their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot edit the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to open the edit editor for that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-002
    Scenario: The author's editor is pre-filled with the current article
      Given a signed-in author with an article titled "Edit Me" tagged "python"
      When they open the edit editor for that article
      Then the editor is pre-filled with "Edit Me"
      And the editor is pre-filled with the tag "python"

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-003
    Scenario: An author edits the summary, body, and tags of their article
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with a new summary, a new body, and the tags "rust"
      Then the article's summary and body are updated
      And the article carries exactly the tag "rust"
      And they are taken to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-EDIT-004
    Scenario: A saved edit cannot leave the title empty
      Given a signed-in author with an existing article
      When they save the editor with an empty title
      Then the editor is shown again for correction

  Rule: Only the author may delete their own article

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-001
    Scenario: A reader who is not the author cannot delete the article
      Given an article authored by someone else
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to delete that article
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DELETE-002
    Scenario: An author deletes their own article
      Given a signed-in author with an article
      When they delete that article
      Then the article no longer exists
      And they are returned to the home feed

  Rule: A draft's detail page is visible only to its author

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-001
    Scenario: An author opens their own draft's detail page
      Given a signed-in author with a draft
      When they open that draft's detail page
      Then the draft is presented

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-002
    Scenario: A different reader cannot open a draft's detail page
      Given an author with a draft
      And a different signed-in reader
      When the reader opens that draft's detail page
      Then the article is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-DRAFT-DETAIL-003
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot open a draft's detail page
      Given an author with a draft
      When an anonymous visitor opens that draft's detail page
      Then the article is reported as not found

  Rule: Favoriting requires sign-in and toggles on each action

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot favorite an article
      When an anonymous visitor tries to favorite an article
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-002
    Scenario: Favoriting then favoriting again removes the favorite
      Given a signed-in reader and an article they have not favorited
      When the reader favorites the article
      Then the article counts the reader among its favorites
      When the reader favorites the article again
      Then the article no longer counts the reader among its favorites

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-003
    Scenario: After a non-HTMX favorite the reader returns to the article
      Given a signed-in reader and an article
      When the reader favorites the article through a full request
      Then they are returned to that article's detail page

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-004
    Scenario: An HTMX favorite returns only the favorite control
      Given a signed-in reader and an article
      When the reader favorites the article via HTMX
      Then only the favorite control fragment is returned

    @RID-ARTICLES-FAVORITE-005
    Scenario: Favoriting a non-existent article is reported as not found
      Given a signed-in reader
      When the reader tries to favorite an article that does not exist
      Then the article is reported as not found

  Rule: A profile page lists a user's own articles or their favorites by tab

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-001
    Scenario: The profile's article tab lists articles written by that user
      Given a user who has written several articles
      When a reader opens that user's profile on the articles tab
      Then the user's own articles are listed newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-002
    Scenario: The profile's favorites tab lists articles that user has favorited
      Given a user who has favorited several articles
      When a reader opens that user's profile on the favorites tab
      Then the articles that user has favorited are listed newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-003
    Scenario: A profile for an unknown user is reported as not found
      When a reader opens a profile for a username that does not exist
      Then the profile is reported as not found

    @RID-ARTICLES-PROFILE-DRAFT-001
    Scenario: The profile's article tab omits the user's drafts
      Given a user with a published article and a draft
      When a reader opens that user's profile on the articles tab
      Then only the published article is listed
      And the draft is not listed

# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` is a boolean that **defaults to `True`** — existing/created articles are public unless explicitly saved as a draft.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Base queryset is filtered to `is_published=True` so **drafts never leak into the global, following, or tag feeds**. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
    - `article_detail_view` treats a draft as private: it renders for the author but returns the standard detail 404 for any other viewer (including anonymous).
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets. The "my articles" tab is a public surface and lists **published articles only** — an author's drafts never appear there (they live in the `?feed=drafts` feed).
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).

# templates/

Django templates. Split into full-page templates and HTMX partials.

## Layout

```
templates/
  base.html              # Root layout — navbar, footer, conduit JS bootstrap
  accounts/              # Full-page templates for the accounts app
    login.html
    register.html
    settings.html
    profile.html         # Used by articles.views.profile_view (not accounts/)
    profile_404.html
  articles/              # Full-page templates for the articles app
    home.html
    detail.html
    detail_404.html
    editor.html
  partials/              # HTMX fragment templates (rendered for HX-Request)
    header.html
    footer.html
    feed_content.html    # The feed portion of home.html — returned for HTMX feed swaps
    article_list.html    # List of article preview cards
    article_meta.html    # Author + date + favorite button for one article
    favorite_button.html # Just the favorite button (swap target)
    follow_button.html   # Just the follow button (swap target)
    comment_list.html    # Entire comment thread (swap target for create/delete)
```

## Conventions

- **Full-page templates** extend `base.html` and are rendered on normal (non-HTMX) requests.
- **Partials** are standalone fragments with no `{% extends %}`. They are returned when `is_htmx(request)` is true, and they are also `{% include %}`-ed by the full-page templates so there is a single source of truth.
- **Swap granularity is the partial**: if HTMX targets `#favorite-button`, the view returns `partials/favorite_button.html` and the server sends just the button. The full-page template also `{% include %}`s the same partial, so the first paint and subsequent swaps render identically.
- **`templates/accounts/profile.html` lives in `accounts/` but is rendered from `articles/views.py::profile_view`**. The template location matches the URL namespace, not the code location. This is intentional (see the `refactor-pass` epic) — don't move it.

## Selectors contract

The RealWorld e2e suite in `realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md` pins specific CSS classes, `name` attributes, and text strings. Before renaming any of the following, grep the SELECTORS contract:

- `<nav class="navbar">`, `<a class="navbar-brand">`, `<a class="nav-link">`
- `input[name="email"]`, `input[name="password"]`, `input[name="username"]`, `input[name="title"]`, `input[name="description"]`, `textarea[name="body"]`, `input[name="image"]`, `textarea[name="bio"]`
- Tab labels `Your Feed`, `Global Feed`, `My Articles`, `Favorited Articles`
- Button text `Sign in`, `Sign up`, `Publish Article`

Breaking these is how you get a working app that fails the e2e suite.

"""Unit tests for articles app — views, models, template tags, management command."""

from io import StringIO
from typing import cast

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from hypothesis import given
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from hypothesis.extra.django import TestCase as HypothesisTestCase

from articles.models import Article
from articles.templatetags.markdown_filter import render_markdown

User = get_user_model()


def make_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw123456", **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(email=email, username=username, password=password, **extra)


def make_article(author, title="A Post", summary="s", content="c", tags=(), is_published=True):
    a = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary=summary, content=content, is_published=is_published)
    for t in tags:
        a.tags.add(t)
    return a


class ArticleModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_save_generates_slug_on_create(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, "hello-world")

    def test_save_does_not_regenerate_slug_on_update(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Hello World", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = a.slug
        a.title = "Totally Different Title"
        a.save()
        self.assertEqual(a.slug, original_slug)

    def test_with_favorites_anonymous_sets_is_favorite_false(self):
        from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser

        user = make_user()
        make_article(user)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(AnonymousUser())
        for art in qs:
            self.assertFalse(art.is_favorite)

    def test_with_favorites_authenticated_reflects_favorites(self):
        alice = make_user()
        bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        a = make_article(alice)
        a.favorites.add(bob)
        qs = Article.objects.with_favorites(bob)
        art = qs.get(pk=a.pk)
        self.assertTrue(art.is_favorite)
        self.assertEqual(art.num_favorites, 1)

    def test_new_article_is_published_by_default(self):
        user = make_user()
        a = Article.objects.create(author=user, title="Fresh Post", summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(a.is_published)


class SlugStabilityPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-SLUG-003: property — any title edit leaves the slug fixed.

    `Article.save()` only regenerates the slug when `self.pk is None`, so once an
    article is created its URL is stable no matter what the title is later set to.
    Each Hypothesis example runs in its own rolled-back transaction, so creating a
    fresh author + article per example is collision-free.
    """

    @given(new_title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_slug_never_changes_on_edit(self, new_title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="slug@example.com", username="sluggy", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title="Original Fixed Title", summary="s", content="c")
        original_slug = article.slug
        article.title = new_title
        article.save()
        self.assertEqual(article.slug, original_slug)


class PublishDefaultPropertyTest(HypothesisTestCase):
    """RID-ARTICLES-PUBLISH-DEFAULT-002: property — any article saved without
    touching the publish flag is published.

    Mirrors SlugStabilityPropertyTest: each Hypothesis example runs in its own
    rolled-back transaction, so a fresh author + article per example is
    collision-free regardless of the (arbitrary) title.
    """

    @given(title=st.text(min_size=1, max_size=140))
    def test_new_article_is_published(self, title):
        author = User.objects.create_user(email="pub@example.com", username="pubby", password="pw123456")
        article = Article.objects.create(author=author, title=title, summary="s", content="c")
        self.assertTrue(article.is_published)


class MarkdownFilterTest(TestCase):
    def test_renders_markdown_and_sanitizes(self):
        html = render_markdown("# Hello\n\n**bold**")
        self.assertIn("<h1>", html)
        self.assertIn("<strong>", html)

    def test_strips_unsafe_html(self):
        html = render_markdown("<script>alert(1)</script>ok")
        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)


class HomeViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        cache.clear()
        self.alice = make_user()
        self.bob = make_user(email="bob@x.com", username="bob")
        self.art1 = make_article(self.alice, title="Post One", tags=["python"])

    def test_anonymous_home_shows_all(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))

        self.assertContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post One")

    def test_following_feed_anonymous_redirects_to_login(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)
        self.assertIn("login", cast(HttpResponseRedirect, resp).url)

    def test_following_feed_authenticated(self):

        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Post Two")
        self.assertEqual(resp.context["active_tab"], "following")

    def test_global_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        make_article(self.alice, title="Secret Draft", is_published=False)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home"))
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Secret Draft")
        self.assertNotIn("Secret Draft", [a.title for a in resp.context["articles"]])

    def test_following_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        self.alice.followers.add(self.bob)  # bob follows alice
        make_article(self.alice, title="Alice Draft", is_published=False)
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?feed=following")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Alice Draft")

    def test_tag_feed_excludes_drafts(self):
        make_article(self.alice, title="Draft Tagged", tags=["python"], is_published=False)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?tag=python")
        self.assertContains(resp, "Post One")
        self.assertNotContains(resp, "Draft Tagged")

    def test_invalid_page_defaults_to_one(self):
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("home") + "?page=bogus")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

Feature: Browsing article feeds
  As a reader
  I want to browse articles through the global feed, my personalised feed, and tag filters
  So that I can discover the writing that matters to me

  The feed is the home surface for articles. A reader can switch between the
  global feed (every article), their personal "following" feed (articles by
  authors they follow), and a tag-filtered view. All three share one feed
  rendering pipeline: the same composition, the same pagination, and the same
  choice between a full page and an in-place fragment refresh.

  Background:
    Given several published articles exist by various authors

  Rule: The global feed shows every article, newest first

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-001
    Scenario: An anonymous reader sees all articles in the global feed
      Given an article "Post One" and an article "Post Two" exist
      When an anonymous reader opens the home feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the global feed

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-002
    Scenario: Articles are ordered newest first
      When a reader opens the global feed
      Then articles appear in order of most recently created first

  Rule: The following feed shows only articles by authors the reader follows

    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-001
    Scenario: A signed-in reader sees only followed authors' articles
      Given a reader who follows the author of "Post One"
      And the author of "Post Two" is not followed by that reader
      When the reader opens their following feed
      Then they see "Post One"
      And they do not see "Post Two"
      And the active tab is the following feed

    # @unverified-intent: anonymous access to the following feed is handled by a
    # server-side redirect to login rather than hiding the tab; documenting the
    # current contract.
    @RID-ARTICLES-FEED-FOLLOWING-002
    Scenario: An anonymous reader requesting the following feed is sent to sign in
      When an anonymous reader requests the following feed
      Then they are redirected to the sign-in page

  Rule: A tag filter narrows the feed to articles carrying that tag

# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`). `is_published` is a boolean that **defaults to `True`** — existing/created articles are public unless explicitly saved as a draft.
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Base queryset is filtered to `is_published=True` so **drafts never leak into the global, following, or tag feeds**. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
    - `article_detail_view` treats a draft as private: it renders for the author but returns the standard detail 404 for any other viewer (including anonymous).
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`) and sets `is_published = not draft`. **Don't rename `title`/`description`/`body`/`tags`** — those are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract. The `draft` checkbox is additive and unchecked by default, so an absent field publishes (the e2e editor flow never sends it).
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets. The "my articles" tab is a public surface and lists **published articles only** — an author's drafts never appear there (they live in the `?feed=drafts` feed).
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`, and `draft`. The first four field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract; `draft` is a `BooleanField(required=False)` checkbox (unchecked = publish, checked = save as draft).
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).
